rule: These methods are listed in this repository. A listing is not a trained model.

methods.name: Causal language modeling
methods.note: Learn next-token prediction from licensed, deduplicated sequences.

methods.name: Masked language modeling
methods.note: Learn bidirectional representations by reconstructing masked tokens.

methods.name: Span-corruption pretraining
methods.note: Reconstruct missing text spans using a text-to-text objective.

methods.name: Denoising autoencoding
methods.note: Reconstruct clean text from governed corruptions and transformations.

methods.name: Contrastive representation learning
methods.note: Learn representations by separating positive and negative views with audited sampling.

methods.name: Multimodal contrastive learning
methods.note: Align licensed image and language representations while measuring subgroup performance.

methods.name: Semi-supervised pseudo-labeling
methods.note: Use filtered teacher labels on unlabeled examples with confidence and bias controls.

methods.name: Transfer learning
methods.note: Adapt reusable representations to a new capability with limited labeled data.

methods.name: Model-agnostic meta-learning
methods.note: Optimize an initialization for rapid adaptation to held-out tasks.

methods.name: Imitation learning
methods.note: Learn actions from expert trajectories while correcting distribution shift with new states.

methods.name: Offline reinforcement learning
methods.note: Learn from a fixed governed behavior dataset without uncontrolled live exploration.

methods.name: Model-based reinforcement learning
methods.note: Learn a bounded world model and evaluate imagined behavior against real holdouts.

methods.name: Evolutionary strategies
methods.note: Compare gradient-free population search with controlled seeds and compute accounting.

methods.name: Sparse mixture-of-experts training
methods.note: Scale expert capacity while measuring routing balance and active compute.

methods.name: Multi-token prediction
methods.note: Predict multiple future tokens with separately validated auxiliary heads.

methods.name: Test-time training
methods.note: Adapt on an auxiliary objective at inference while isolating and rolling back each session update.

methods.name: Test-time compute scaling
methods.note: Allocate search and verification compute based on measured problem difficulty.

methods.name: Knowledge-graph embedding
methods.note: Learn structured entity relations while retaining provenance to source records.

methods.name: Continued pretraining
methods.note: Continue next-token learning on a governed, licensed corpus.

methods.name: Domain-adaptive pretraining
methods.note: Adapt a base model to a bounded domain before task tuning.

methods.name: Retrieval-augmented training
methods.note: Train retrieval and generation against attributable knowledge sources.

methods.name: Curriculum learning
methods.note: Order examples from easier foundations to harder capabilities.

methods.name: Self-paced learning
methods.note: Let measured competence control when harder examples enter training.

methods.name: Active learning
methods.note: Request labels for examples expected to reduce uncertainty most.

methods.name: Hard-example mining
methods.note: Concentrate study on repeatable failure clusters without discarding easy regression cases.

methods.name: Deduplication and quality filtering
methods.note: Remove duplicates, contamination, low-quality text, and unsafe or unlicensed records.

methods.name: Multilingual data balancing
methods.note: Measure and rebalance language coverage instead of allowing majority-language collapse.

methods.name: Synthetic self-instruction
methods.note: Generate, filter, and deduplicate candidate instructions before supervised use.

methods.name: Synthetic curriculum
methods.note: Generate progressively harder examples, then filter them with independent graders and contamination checks.

methods.name: Rejection sampling
methods.note: Keep generated examples only when independent graders and policy filters pass.

methods.name: Cold-start supervised fine-tuning
methods.note: Seed readable reasoning behavior before reinforcement learning.

methods.name: Instruction tuning
methods.note: Train across natural-language instructions and held-out task families.

methods.name: Multitask supervised fine-tuning
methods.note: Mix capability families with explicit sampling and retention checks.

methods.name: Reasoning-trace supervised tuning
methods.note: Teach structured reasoning examples while grading only observable outputs and authorized traces.

methods.name: Tool-use supervised tuning
methods.note: Teach when and how to call tools using sandbox-verifiable outcomes.

methods.name: Tool-use learning
methods.note: Combine supervised examples, filtered self-generated calls, and verifiable tool outcomes.

methods.name: LoRA adapter tuning
methods.note: Learn bounded low-rank updates without overwriting the base checkpoint.

methods.name: QLoRA adapter tuning
methods.note: Fine-tune adapters through a quantized frozen base model.

methods.name: Adapter fusion
methods.note: Compose separately learned skills while keeping their artifacts reversible.

methods.name: RLHF with PPO
methods.note: Optimize against a human-feedback reward model with a reference-policy constraint.

methods.name: Reinforcement learning from AI feedback
methods.note: Use constitutionally guided model feedback with human validation and bias checks.

methods.name: Direct preference optimization
methods.note: Learn pairwise preferences without a separately fitted reward model.

methods.name: Preference-optimization study
methods.note: Compare preference objectives on identical data, seeds, graders, and release gates.

methods.name: Identity preference optimization
methods.note: Test a regularized preference objective against DPO on identical fixtures.

methods.name: KTO preference optimization
methods.note: Learn from desirable and undesirable examples when pairs are unavailable.

methods.name: ORPO preference optimization
methods.note: Compare a monolithic preference objective with staged SFT and alignment.

methods.name: Group-relative policy optimization
methods.note: Estimate relative group advantages without a separate critic model.

methods.name: RL with verifiable rewards
methods.note: Reward answers only when code, math, or tool outcomes are independently verifiable.

methods.name: Process reward modeling
methods.note: Grade intermediate solution steps with contamination and reward-hacking checks.

methods.name: Outcome reward modeling
methods.note: Grade final observable outcomes and compare against process supervision.

methods.name: STaR self-taught reasoning
methods.note: Generate rationales, keep independently correct examples, and iterate on failures.

methods.name: Quiet-STaR
methods.note: Study whether token-level internal rationales improve general text prediction.

methods.name: Self-consistency decoding
methods.note: Sample diverse reasoning paths and aggregate answers for evaluation or filtered data.

methods.name: Self-critique and revision
methods.note: Use explicit feedback, retry limits, and external graders to revise failed attempts.

methods.name: Multi-agent debate
methods.note: Compare independent arguments while controlling correlated-model and judge bias.

methods.name: Tool-augmented reasoning
methods.note: Learn tool selection from real sandbox results rather than persuasive text alone.

methods.name: Continual experience replay
methods.note: Replay representative prior capabilities during new-skill learning.

methods.name: Elastic weight consolidation
methods.note: Penalize changes to parameters important for retained capabilities.

methods.name: Modular skill adapters
methods.note: Keep capability updates modular, scoped, removable, and independently benchmarked.

methods.name: Federated learning
methods.note: Aggregate bounded updates without centralizing raw participant data.

methods.name: Evaluation-triggered learning
methods.note: Open a learning proposal from clustered failures, never silently change production weights.

methods.name: Teacher-student distillation
methods.note: Transfer calibrated teacher behavior into a smaller student on licensed examples.

methods.name: Progressive distillation
methods.note: Distill in measured stages while enforcing a quality and retention floor.

methods.name: Policy distillation
methods.note: Transfer a stronger policy into a compact policy with task-level evaluation.

methods.name: Quantization-aware training
methods.note: Adapt to reduced precision while measuring quality and latency tradeoffs.

methods.name: Structured pruning
methods.note: Remove bounded structures and require before-and-after capability evidence.

methods.name: Hyperband
methods.note: Stop weak configurations early and allocate budget to promising trials.

methods.name: Bayesian hyperparameter optimization
methods.note: Choose new trials from uncertainty-aware estimates of the objective.

methods.name: Population-based training
methods.note: Evolve schedules and parameters while preserving complete lineage.

methods.name: Controlled ablation
methods.note: Change one component at a time to identify what caused an improvement.

methods.name: Multi-armed-bandit strategy selection
methods.note: Balance exploration of uncertain techniques with exploitation of efficient ones.

methods.name: Pareto multi-objective selection
methods.note: Reject a single vanity score and retain quality, safety, cost, latency, and readability tradeoffs.

methods.name: Spaced Repetition
methods.note: Revisit skills on expanding intervals to retain mastery.

methods.name: Active Recall
methods.note: Test retrieval instead of re-reading notes.

methods.name: Interleaving
methods.note: Mix related skill types in one practice block.

methods.name: Deliberate Practice
methods.note: Target weakest subskill with immediate feedback.

methods.name: Error Analysis
methods.note: Cluster failures by root cause; fix causes not symptoms.

methods.name: Curriculum Learning
methods.note: Train from easy → hard examples.

methods.name: Contrastive Learning
methods.note: Learn boundaries by comparing good vs bad examples.

methods.name: Meta-Learning
methods.note: Learn which strategy works for which task class.

methods.name: Reinforcement from Feedback
methods.note: Increase weight of actions that earn positive outcomes.

methods.name: Imitation Learning
methods.note: Clone expert traces (approved human or golden runs).

methods.name: Self-Play / Self-Challenge
methods.note: Generate harder variants of tasks you already pass.

methods.name: Knowledge Distillation
methods.note: Compress long traces into short playbooks and prompts.

methods.name: Human-in-the-Loop Correction
methods.note: Owner edits become supervised labels for future runs.

methods.name: Benchmark-Driven Improvement
methods.note: Close the lowest failing benchmark dimension first.

methods.name: Multi-Perspective Study
methods.note: Study the same problem from code, product, risk, and user views.

methods.name: Dependency Reduction Learning
methods.note: Prefer local/native skills over external paid dependencies.

methods.name: Failure Memory
methods.note: Persist failure signatures so the same mistake is not repeated.

methods.name: Bootcamp Mastery Gates
methods.note: Progress only after lesson checks pass.

methods.name: Transfer Learning
methods.note: Apply skills from one division/bot to a related domain.

methods.name: Continuous Learning Cycle
methods.note: Observe → hypothesize → test in sandbox → measure → promote or discard.
